**The fork is realigned onto upstream open-gsd v1.20.1.** That is 20 upstream commits, merged with 53 conflicts resolved, all of them mechanical (version fields, fork identity and generated files). It is the eighth merge-anchored realignment. Everything below is new since fork 2.9.0.

What v1.20.1 brings, and what the fork does about each:

- **Installs into a nested or unusually named config directory keep correct paths on every runtime (#5715).** A `--config-dir` such as `~/.claude/profiles/work`, `~/.claude.d` or `~/.copilot/work` was rewritten again inside its own output, and a `$&` in a config dir was expanded. Each `~/.claude` reference is now rewritten once, and later converters no longer touch the emitted prefix. Across default global and local installs of every runtime, only one output changes: a Trae local install points its skills at the project's `.trae/` instead of the global `~/.trae/`. Upstream also lists a Windsurf skills-path fix and keeping Claude Code's own `~/.claude.json` and `.claude-plugin` names. Those two changes are in the shared rewrite helper, and no file this fork ships contains those paths. If a workflow or agent did contain them, the install for several runtimes would still rename Claude Code's file names (for example to `~/.cline.json` or `~/.codex.json`), exactly as upstream v1.20.1 does. The fork's own install-time transforms (the `argument-hint` carry on Codex and Cursor skills, the verbatim emit of the certification reference, the brand-swap hardening) rewrite no paths, so they add no second pass. Installs of this build for Claude Code, Kilo, Codex and OpenCode under `~/.claude/profiles/work-*` were checked. No emitted file, fork commands and agents included, repeats the prefix.
- **`effort sync --apply` no longer makes the next install back up synced agents as local patches (#5683).** The sync now records the new hashes in `gsd-file-manifest.json`. That covers the agents that carry fork content: syncing `gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-executor` and `gsd-roadmapper` and then reinstalling created no `gsd-local-patches/`.
- **Milestone-prefixed phase ids (`phase_id_convention: milestone-prefixed`) are read whole (#5675, #5676).** `phase complete`, `state sync`, init progress, `find-phase`, the planning snapshot, `drift-guard phase-status` and workstream progress now read `3-02` as phase `3-02`. Before, they read it as milestone `3`. `phase insert` names the milestone that holds a phase from another milestone instead of saying it is missing (#5679). The fork's `context verify` already resolves phases through upstream's phase locator, so it reads these ids the same way.
- **Two orchestrators in one checkout no longer refuse each other's dispatches (#5682).** Each dispatch's isolation decision is now kept for its own phase and plan.
- **The tool-owned `.gsd/` directory has one owner (#5757).** It refuses a `.gsd` symlink that leads outside the project and ignores itself in git, so a fresh project no longer shows `.gsd/` as untracked. The fork's learn visual companion now stores `--project-dir` session files through the same owner. It refuses such a symlink, which keeps the session key inside the project. On a fresh project `.gsd/.gitignore` is `*`, which already ignores the session files. If you wrote your own `.gsd/.gitignore` without a `*` line, the companion appends `/learn-visual/` and `/.gitignore` to it and keeps your rules.
- **The new-project and new-milestone hand-off names the right next step (#5723).** Upstream now recommends `/gsd-discuss-phase`, with `/gsd-plan-phase` to plan directly and `/gsd-execute-phase` to execute. In this fork the hand-off still starts with the strategy chain. After `/gsd-new-project`, run the first step your `## Strategy Plan` recommends; the chain ends by creating the roadmap with `/gsd-roadmap`. If no step is recommended, run `/gsd-roadmap` directly. After `/gsd-new-milestone`, the milestone's first recommended strategy step comes first. Upstream's discuss → plan → execute wording applies once the roadmap exists.

Fork-side changes in this realignment:

- **`/gsd-learn` starts its visual companion again.** Step 5 looked for the start script under the project root instead of the install, so the companion never started on any runtime and every lesson fell back to text. It now starts the script that ships with the installed gsd-core.
- **`/gsd-roadmap` hands off to the active milestone's next phase instead of phase 1.** It reads the phase from `roadmap analyze`. Before, the end of a `/gsd-new-milestone` strategy chain sent `/gsd-discuss-phase` to the archived phase 1 of the shipped milestone. On a project with milestone-prefixed ids (`1-01`), the chain stopped at "Phase 1 not found".
- **`/gsd-legacy-inventory` continues the strategy chain on a project that is already initialized.** When `/gsd-new-milestone` recommends it, it now moves on to the next `## Strategy Plan` step, or to `/gsd-roadmap` when none is left. Before, it handed off to `/gsd-new-project`, which stopped with "project already initialized".
- **A `map-codebase` row in `## Strategy Plan` counts as done once the codebase map is complete** (all seven documents in `.planning/codebase/`). `/gsd-map-codebase` does not mark its row, so `/gsd-next` used to route back to it after mapping.
- **`/gsd-next` puts the new milestone's strategy step first.** This applies when `/gsd-new-milestone` recommended a step and no phase of the milestone is planned yet. The discuss and plan actions stay in the menu.
- **The `/gsd-new-project` description no longer lists `ROADMAP.md` and `STATE.md` among the files it creates.** `/gsd-roadmap` writes them at the end of the strategy chain.
- **The fork's own skip of the emitted-attribution gate on release → main PRs is retired.** Upstream now measures a release-merge PR from its fork point on `next` (#5902), which is the range the skip was protecting. A simulated `release/2.10.0` → `main` PR on this tree passes the gate without the skip.
- **Release pipeline (#5894, #5890, #5903):** `release.yml` refuses `create` and `finalize` unless `main` is an ancestor of `next`. The fork's history passes that check: its back-merges land as merge commits. Upstream's issue-link, title and changeset-lint exemptions recognise `release/A.B.0` → `main`. The issue-link and title checks load that rule from the base branch, so on the fork they take effect from the promotion after this one, once `main` carries the rule. They do not recognise the fork's `chore/backmerge-A.B.0-to-next` branch, because upstream expects `chore/backmerge-main-to-next-<sha>`. Those checks will keep failing on the fork's back-merge PRs. That is expected and does not block the merge.
- **The three known issues listed for 2.9.0 are not addressed by upstream 1.20.1.** All three still apply: the `--reset-phase-numbers` Progress row, the bracket checklist tick, and uninstall removing your own `skills/gsd-*` directories.
